summary: Tested resolve_template_variables() in scheduler.py for {vehicle}/{purchase} template logic. {vehicle} resolution from purchase_history, {purchase} alias, and most-recent-sort all PASS. But found a critical Python operator precedence bug on line 149 that breaks {first_name} resolution when contact dict has no 'contact_name' key.

critical.issue: Python operator precedence bug: `contact_first = (contact.get('first_name') or contact.get('contact_name','').split()[0] if contact.get('contact_name') else 'there')` — the ternary has higher precedence than `or`, so entire expression evaluates as `(X if contact.get('contact_name') else 'there')`. When a contact dict has first_name='John' but no 'contact_name' key, {first_name} resolves to 'there' instead of 'John'. Fix: add explicit parentheses: `contact_first = contact.get('first_name') or (contact.get('contact_name','').split()[0] if contact.get('contact_name') else 'there')`

action_items: Fix line 149 in /app/backend/scheduler.py: change `contact_first = (contact.get('first_name') or contact.get('contact_name', '').split()[0] if contact.get('contact_name') else 'there')` to `contact_first = contact.get('first_name') or (contact.get('contact_name', '').split()[0] if contact.get('contact_name') else 'there')`
critical_code_review_comments: scheduler.py line 149: Python operator precedence bug — ternary (`if/else`) has higher precedence than `or`, making the whole expression conditional on `contact_name` presence. This silently breaks {first_name} for any contact fetched via find_one() that doesn't have a contact_name field (which is the normal case for DB contacts).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Tests in /app/backend/tests/test_vehicle_template.py cover all 5 vehicle/purchase scenarios. 4/6 pass. 2 fail due to {first_name} resolving to 'there' (line 149 bug). After E1 fixes line 149, rerun the same test file — all 6 should pass.

rca_of_the_issue.bug: {first_name} resolves to 'there' instead of contact's actual first_name
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: Python operator precedence: `A or B if C else D` parses as `(A or B) if C else D`, not `A or (B if C else D)`. So the entire expression is gated on `contact.get('contact_name')` being truthy. When a DB contact has first_name='John' but no contact_name field, it falls through to 'there'.
rca_of_the_issue.fix: Line 149: `contact_first = contact.get('first_name') or (contact.get('contact_name', '').split()[0] if contact.get('contact_name') else 'there')`
